Nia (CS): Sable Ops aiming for private deployment cutover next Wed 08:00 PT. Quick preflight 3 want owners to confirm network, IAM, KMS, and audit-log readiness. Blockers?

Sable Ops: Dry-run tomorrow. Questions: 1) can Redwood write to our compliance S3 with Object Lock enabled? 2) who holds the CMK by default? 3) what maintenance IPs to allow?

Axel (Network): We'll provide maintenance CIDRs and route table entries. Peering is simplest; recommend peering for initial go-live.

Bea (Security): We prefer customer-managed CMKs for auditability. If you want Redwood-managed for now, we can offer a dedicated key. For Object Locked buckets, Redwood needs PutObjectRetention and PutObjectLegalHold permissions. Also need CloudTrail enabled for KMS events.

Theo (SRE): SRE checklist: peering + routes, DNS resolving internal endpoints, healthcheck (tcp/9443) reachable from your subnets. Smoke test: `curl -H "X-Test: smoke" https://api.internal.redwood/health --resolve api.internal.redwood:443:10.10.8.7`

Sable Ops: Bucket ARN: arn:aws:s3:::sable-compliance-logs. Retention: 6y WORM. Legal asks that CMK ownership can be reassigned after 120 days.

onboard-bot: Checklist items added: vpc-peering, routes, dns, healthcheck, cmk-policy, s3-trust-role, object-lock-perms, post-cut runbook. Status: 0/8.

Axel (Network): Posting CIDRs in 5m and a tiny terraform snippet for peering.

Bea (Security): I'll drop CMK policy and S3 trust policy templates to the ticket; include least-privilege guidance for object lock.

Theo (SRE): I'll prepare the post-cut dashboard (p50/p95, 5xx rate, auth fails) and a 90-minute rollback plan.

Nia (CS): I'll coordinate legal on the 120-day CMK clause and produce the 1-pager runbook post dry-run. If owners are green, react with :thumbsup:.

Axel (Network): :thumbsup:

Bea (Security): :thumbsup:

Theo (SRE): :thumbsup:

Sable Ops: :thumbsup: see you at the dry-run.
